motion.name: seal-verify

motion.name: walk

motion.name: proof-surfaces
motion.purpose: Ledger, counters, top bar and every number never animate; no proof surface ever moves.

motion.name: command-drill

motion.name: command-drawer
motion.purpose: Forensic drawer fading and sliding in from the right on Command.

motion.name: seam-snap
motion.purpose: Seal halves close from 8 to 0 units of the mark's 256 grid in 8 frames at 60 fps and stop dead: no overshoot, no settle; the green seam is lit from the first frame.

motion.name: mismatch-open
motion.purpose: On a denial the halves part from 8 to 16 units in 6 frames and stay apart; the Alert bar replaces the seam from the first frame.

motion.name: mismatch-shake
motion.purpose: Four lateral beats of 6 units, left first (-6, +6, -6, +6), then still from 320 ms.

motion.name: alert-enter
motion.purpose: The alert bar fades from opacity 0 to 1 in its final box, together with the seal's verdict; nothing slides.

motion.name: bubble-enter
motion.purpose: Sentence bubbles fade from opacity 0 to 1 in their final box.

motion.name: explorer-settle
motion.purpose: Explorer verdict, step discs and marks change colour; nothing moves.

motion.name: holder-arrive

motion.name: holder-funds-delay
motion.purpose: The funds stamp lands this long after its paper, so the verified line settles last.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every CSS transition and animation is stilled and the world stops drifting; the seal's wait, verify and deny states still land at once.

narrative.overview:
The console is one small pixel world seen through a dark frame. Meta's agents work in an office on the left, the bank branch sits on the right, and between them stands a teller booth with the Mandate seal on its face. Every request walks to that window. A verified request joins the seal's halves with a green seam. An attack is refused: the halves shake apart, a red bar drops under the booth, and the intruder is thrown back. Everything around the world is dark security: Ink ground, Bone monospace labels, one-pixel hairlines, and a ledger of real events below.

The pixel world carries the warmth and the motion. The chrome stays quiet so the verdict at the booth is always the loudest thing on screen. Text is never painted into the world: tags, bubbles, the alert, the sign and every ledger cell are live DOM text set over the canvas, so they stay sharp, selectable and spoken. The brand commitments behind the palette and type (Ink and Bone, Verify reserved for verified states, Inter with JetBrains Mono, "dark security + pixel soul") are stated in `PRODUCT.md`. The surface's direction contract is `.impeccable/surfaces/console-index-html.md`.

The same world reaches four more surfaces, each quieter than the last. Command (`console/command.html`) is the posture register with no scene. The explorer (`console/explorer.html`) is the teller window seen from the public side, with the small booth as its only scene element. The holder page (`console/holder.html`) is a cheque written on the holder's own phone. The glasses page (`webapp/`) is a 600×600 glance on a pure black ground. All five share one base: Ink and Bone, the 2px Bone focus ring, Bone selection, Muted scrollbars, and the readability floor below.
keyCharacteristics: An integer-scaled 444×164 pixel world at the centre of the first viewport, the booth always centred.
A 16-colour duotone-green world palette, separate from the UI palette.
Green means verified and red means refused, and nothing else uses either.
Square Ink tags with Bone monospace text, and no rounded bubbles.
One authored motion moment, the seal's verdict. The world drifts on its own; the proof surfaces never move.
Every text run is at least 14px at 1440×900, and every hero signal at least 18px.

rules.name: The Green Means Verified Rule
rules.body: Verify appears only where a gate decision verified something. A denied count stays Bone.

rules.name: The Two Palettes Rule
rules.body: UI colours never enter the world, and world colours never style the UI. The one bridge is the booth face, which the seal borrows from the plate.

rules.name: The Withheld Is Not A Verdict Rule
rules.body: A field that was not checked against anything is an Ink chip ringed in Muted (2px inset) with its word in Muted. It never takes Verify, Alert or the Muted fill of a link left unchecked, so it reads as neither a pass, a failure nor a skipped step.

rules.name: The Readability Floor Rule
rules.body: At 1440×900 every text run on every console page is at least 14px, and every hero signal (the verdict, the amount, a metric value, the alert at 3×) is at least 18px. In-world type follows the stage scale but never drops under 14px. Only narrower layouts step below the floor: Command's compact tables at 1100–1380px (13.5px, with 12px in their longest column); and at ≤720px Command's provenance line (13px) and stacked column names (10.5px), and the explorer's step numbers and marks (13px).

rules.name: The Live Text Rule
rules.body: No word is ever drawn into the pixels. Every word is DOM text over the canvas, so a screen reader, a selection and a zoom all reach it.

rules.name: The Tracking Floor Rule
rules.body: Mono is never tracked tighter than −0.04em.

rules.name: The Integer Pixel Rule
rules.body: The world is only ever drawn at a whole-number scale, with `image-rendering: pixelated`, `imageSmoothingEnabled = false` and every draw at a whole native pixel. Never stretch the stage to fill a width; crop it around the booth.

rules.name: The Flat Chrome Rule
rules.body: No shadows, glass or glows on UI. If something needs to stand forward, it gets Ink behind it and a Bone hairline around it.

rules.name: The Alert Only On Breach Rule
rules.body: On Command, Refusal Red appears only where an attack was not blocked or moved money, a Nimbus step ran when it should not, or a payment had no bank backing: those counts, their cents, the words `not stopped`, an unbacked bank check, and a total that falls short. Blocked counts and zero values stay Bone, and the words always say it as well as the colour.

rules.name: The Real Columns Rule
rules.body: Every number on Command comes from a line in the window or from this process's registry and policies. A column the approved design did not draw stays if the data has it; a value the design invented never ships.

dos: **Do** draw the world at an integer scale and crop it around the booth when it does not fit.
**Do** snap every plate and frame to the 16 world colours before shipping it, and embed its generation prompt and request id in the PNG.
**Do** carry pass and deny in words and shape as well as colour: VERIFIED / DENIED, the joined or split seal, the struck hash.
**Do** put Ink text on Refusal Red, never Bone.
**Do** label honest seams: `template attack` against `open-weights attacker`, TEMPLATE against MODEL, the layer that refused.
**Do** keep every word as live text over the canvas.
**Do** give every focusable element the 2px Bone ring offset 2px (4px on the glasses page).
**Do** hold every text run at 14px or more at 1440×900, and every hero signal at 18px or more.
**Do** mark a withheld field as an Ink chip with a Muted ring and a Muted word.
donts: **Don't** use Verify Green for anything but a verified decision.
**Don't** animate the ledger, the counters or any number. Motion belongs to the verdict and the world.
**Don't** add cards, rounded bubbles, shadows or containers around the world. Tags are square Ink.
**Don't** smooth, stretch or sub-pixel-position the world.
**Don't** paint words into a plate. The booth sign is DOM text.
**Don't** track mono tighter than −0.04em, or set world type under 14px.
**Don't** use pure black anywhere but the glasses page's ground.
**Don't** load or set a weight the system does not ship (Inter 400/700/800, JetBrains Mono 400/700, Press Start 2P 400).
